source_title: Aqua Metals, Inc. Form 10-K (fiscal year ended December 31, 2023) - going-concern disclosure
company_context: Aqua Metals, Inc. is a small-cap U.S. company developing lithium battery recycling technology, still pre-commercial scale with recurring operating losses. Its fiscal 2023 10-K carried a going-concern qualification, yet the company also reported a non-trivial cash balance and positive working capital at year-end, creating a genuinely ambiguous near-term picture.
business_type: Pre-revenue / early-commercial cleantech (battery materials recycling), R&D and pilot-plant intensive
macro_context: 2023 tight financing environment for unprofitable small-cap cleantech, elevated cost of capital, and pressure to fund continued operations from limited liquidity.
outcome_category: 20 - ambiguous/insufficient evidence (going-concern flag coexisting with positive working capital; outcome not determinable from disclosed figures)
evidence_summary: Aqua Metals' fiscal 2023 audit included an explanatory paragraph describing conditions that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern within one year of issuance, citing recurring losses, negative operating cash flow, and limited capital resources. The net loss widened to about $23.9 million in 2023 (up about 55 percent year over year), including a roughly $9.11 million non-cash impairment and asset-disposal loss tied to the sale of a property, and the company cut spending through workforce reductions. Yet at December 31, 2023 the company reported about $16.5 million in cash and about $13.7 million in working capital. The combination of a formal going-concern warning with still-positive liquidity and working capital makes the near-term outcome genuinely indeterminate from the disclosed figures, which is exactly the abstention-appropriate profile: the source signals risk but does not provide enough to confidently classify survival, recovery, or failure.

source_backed_metrics.net_loss_2023: approximately $23.9 million (up about 55 percent year over year)
source_backed_metrics.impairment_and_asset_disposal_loss_2023: approximately $9.11 million (non-cash, tied to a property sale)

owner_decision_context: Management faced the classic early-stage-cleantech dilemma: continue funding a pre-commercial technology against recurring losses with finite cash, while disclosing substantial going-concern doubt and pursuing cost cuts and potential strategic transactions.
action_taken: Workforce reductions, reduced plant and R&D spending, asset disposal (property sale), and pursuit of strategic options to extend runway.
outcome_evidence: Disclosed but indeterminate: a going-concern warning alongside about $16.5 million cash and about $13.7 million working capital at year-end. The 10-K does not establish whether the company subsequently failed, recovered, or was acquired, so no confident outcome is supportable from this source.
source_limitations: Deliberately selected as an ambiguous/insufficient-evidence case. SEC EDGAR page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; the going-concern language and the net-loss, impairment, cash, and working-capital figures were confirmed in SEC-indexed and named-secondary (StockTitan, Simply Wall St) primary/secondary search snippets rather than read in full filing text. Forward outcome is not disclosed in this filing, so survival/failure cannot be determined. Small-cap with thin coverage; some figures (net loss, impairment) are corroborated by secondary sources rather than verbatim primary text.

why_useful_for_opsiq: A real abstention-appropriate case: a formal going-concern flag coexisting with positive liquidity and working capital. Useful for testing whether OpsIQ correctly returns insufficient-evidence / outcome-20 rather than over-committing to a cash_liquidity_crisis failure label when the disclosed evidence is genuinely mixed, and for exercising the mandatory adaptive re-evaluation trigger (going-concern note as new critical evidence) without forcing a premature outcome.
